<!-- Load when: parsing a filed sprint report, or any other run evidence, from outside the skill -->

The published shape of the evidence a run leaves behind, versioned apart from the skill so a parser can tell what an upgrade moved.

> **Annex version 1.1.** The artefact format is contracted in
> [reference-schema.md](reference-schema.md); this annex contracts the evidence records that
> page leaves out. Each record type has its own heading below.

## Versioning

The annex carries its own version, starting at 1.0, and moves only when an evidence shape moves:
a skill release that changes no record leaves it alone. A change a parser can ignore, such as a
new key, section, row key or envelope mark, raises the minor version. A change that removes or
renames a key, changes a rule mark's value or a figure's shape, or adds a report schema raises
the major version.

Every report page `sprint close` files, and every run record committed beside it, states the
version it was written under as `evidence_schema`, in major.minor form. The close stamps the
page as it derives it, and the run record copies the stamp from the page it names, so a run
signed after an upgrade keeps the version its page was stamped with. A page filed before the
stamp carries no `evidence_schema`, nor does its run record, and the page still checks.

A consumer must tolerate unknown keys: an added field is a minor bump, so a parser written
against one minor version reads a later one by passing over what it does not know. A removed or
renamed field is a major bump and carries a migration note in this annex, under the heading of
the record it moved, naming the old key, the new one and the version that moved it.

## Reading the tables

Every contract on this page is a Markdown table under a fixed heading, and each row names its
key in a code span in the row's first key column. A parser reads the heading, then the table
beneath it, and treats the prose around the tables as explanation only. The suite reads the
tables the same way and holds them to the records the skill writes.

## Report of record

The JSON page `sprint close` files as `sdlc-studio/reports/RPTnnnn.json` is the record. The
Markdown twin committed beside it and the HTML that `sprint_report.py render` produces are
renderings of it, and are not contracted: their wording and layout may change in any release.

### Report schemas

The envelope's `schema` key says which shape a page has. Pages under every schema stay in the
tree, so a parser meets both.

| Schema | Written by | Re-derivable | Check answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `1` | no writer: the first shape, held only by pages already filed | no | `sprint_report.py check` exits 2, saying the page cannot be re-derived and the page stands as filed |
| `2` | `sprint close` | yes | `sprint_report.py check` reads `VALID` when the page re-derives to the fingerprint it records, and otherwise names each figure that moved |

### Report envelope keys

The top-level keys of a schema-2 page. **Presence** is `always`; `rule mark`, a key every page
filed since its rule took effect carries, so a page without it was filed before the rule and is
re-derived without it; or `conditional`, with the condition in the meaning. A **Value** in a
code span is the only value the key takes.

| Key | Presence | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | always | `2` | The report schema the page was filed under. |
| `evidence_schema` | rule mark | this annex's version, as major.minor | The annex version the page was filed under, under the rule in Versioning. Outside the fingerprint. |
| `report_id` | always | the page's id | The id the report index files the page under. |
| `run_id` | always | the run's id | The run the page reports. |
| `retro_id` | always | the retro's id | The retro the close was run against. |
| `generated_at` | always | an ISO 8601 time | When the page was derived. Outside the fingerprint. |
| `window_end` | always | an ISO 8601 time | The end of the window the figures measure to, replayed on every re-derivation. |
| `signature` | always | null, or the signature block | Null until `sprint sign` signs the page. Outside the fingerprint. |
| `sections` | always | a list | The sections, in the order of the section catalogue. |
| `findings_window_end` | conditional | an ISO 8601 time | Present when a re-close bounded the open findings, waivers and DORA later than `window_end`. |
| `record_paths` | rule mark | `portable` | The page was derived from the run record as the tracked copy holds it. |
| `token_ratio` | rule mark | `every-delivered-unit-delegated` | The tokens ratio is withheld over a partial delegated actual. |
| `restore_pairing` | rule mark | `next-success-after-failure` | Time to restore pairs each failure with the next success. |
| `discharged_carry` | rule mark | `delivered` | A carried unit discharged in the run counts as delivered. |
| `findings_scan` | rule mark | `delivered-batch-units-excluded` | The open findings leave out the run's own delivered units. |
| `minutes_ratio` | rule mark | `measured-unit-minutes` | Measured minutes are compared with the forecast. |
| `delegated_tokens` | rule mark | `counted-over-a-zero-meter` | Delegated totals count even where the session meter read 0. |
| `agent_minutes` | rule mark | `any-agent-supplied` | A unit's agent minutes are read when any agent supplied them. |
| `dora_failures` | rule mark | `failure-or-timed-out-only` | A cancelled or skipped CI run is not a failed deployment. |
| `token_headline` | rule mark | `priced-input-equivalent` | The token rows lead with the priced cost. |
| `priced_units` | rule mark | `unit-priced-and-per-point` | The priced cost per delivered point and per unit are stated. |
| `usd_cost` | rule mark | `per-model-dollars-and-roles` | Dollars, premium requests and the spend by role are stated. |
| `price_table` | conditional | an object | Present when the price table could be read: the prices the dollar figures were formed from. |
| `price_table_rule` | conditional | `replayed-and-digested` | Present beside `price_table`: the table is replayed on re-derivation and is inside the fingerprint. |
| `premium_usd` | rule mark | `per-request-dollars` | Premium requests are priced per request. |
| `usd_prices` | rule mark | `per-model-prices-and-delegated-dollars` | Each priced model's prices are listed and the delegated totals priced. |
| `cost_forecast` | rule mark | `forecast-actual-ratio` | The Priced cost, Priced per point, Dollar cost, Dollars per point and Wall-clock span rows state the plan's forecast and actual over forecast, or why none was made. |
| `dispatch_effort` | rule mark | `per-role-from-plan` | The cost section states the effort each unit's builder and reviewer were dispatched at; a builder a headless lane ran with no effort flag under a stamp other than `inherit` is stated as configured and not applied. |
| `fingerprint` | always | a hex digest | The digest of the page's figure set, which a signature is over. |

### Report section shape

Every entry of `sections` is an object with these keys.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | The section's key in the section catalogue. |
| `title` | The heading the renderings print. |
| `figures` | An object of figures by figure key; empty when the section has none. |
| `rows` | A list of rows, each an object of figures by row key; empty when there are none. |
| `unit_rows` | The per-unit rows, on the estimates section. |
| `not_measured` | Null, or a figure reading `NOT MEASURED` whose reason says why the section could not be measured. |

### Report figure shape

Every figure, in `figures`, in a row or as `not_measured`, is an object with these fields.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `key` | The figure's key: the key it is stored under, or the section's key for `not_measured`. |
| `value` | A number or a string. A measurement nobody could take reads `NOT MEASURED`, never 0 or empty. |
| `source` | Where the figure can be re-derived from, under the source grammar below. |
| `reason` | Why the figure reads `NOT MEASURED`, where it does. |
| `label` | A qualifier printed after a `unit_rows` figure read from the agents tagged to the unit, beginning `agent minutes`, `agent tokens`, `priced` or `estimated`. Absent on every other figure. |

### Report source grammar

A figure's `source` is one source, or several joined by a comma followed by a space. Each part
is one of four kinds:

1. A declared non-path source: the part begins with one of the sources in the first table
   below, a command whose output was read or a place the workspace does not hold.
2. A file that exists in the workspace.
3. A workspace path: the part begins with one of the prefixes in the second table below. It
   may name a file nothing has written yet, such as a ledger a run with no entries never
   created, because that absence is what the figure reports.
4. A path ending in `.jsonl` outside the workspace, such as a session transcript the harness
   owns.

A page never carries a figure whose source is empty or is none of these: the build refuses
it.

#### Report non-path sources

| Source | What it names |
| --- | --- |
| `gh run list` | The forge's CI runs, read with the GitHub CLI. |
| `git log` | The repository's history. |
| `git history` | The repository's history. |
| `the session transcript` | The harness session the meter read. |
| `forge run` | A CI run the forge reported. |
| `forge runs` | The CI runs the forge reported. |
| `the harness meter` | The token meter the harness keeps. |
| `no forge` | No forge was reachable, so the figure was read without one. |
| `the skill's bundled seed` | The lesson classes the skill ships, read when the project has no class store. |

#### Report workspace prefixes

| Prefix | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `sdlc-studio/` | The workspace's artefacts, ledgers and run records. |
| `.claude/` | The installed skill. |
| `tools/` | The project's own tools. |
| `docs/` | The project's documentation. |
| `changelog.d/` | Changelog fragments. |

### Report fingerprint

The envelope's `fingerprint` is a digest of the page's figure set, not of the file, so recording
a signature on the page never changes what the signature is over. The signature block, the
generation time and each figure's source are not signed: only each figure's `value` enters the
digest, and of the rest of the envelope only the price table does, on a page that replays it.
This is the schema-2 fingerprint; a schema-1 page's fingerprint is not catalogued. Read the page
keeping every object's keys in the order the page holds them, then:

1. Walk `sections` in page order. From each section take its `not_measured` figure, when it is
   present and not null, under the key `not_measured`; then each entry of `figures` in page
   order, under its figure key; then each row of `rows`, then each row of `unit_rows`, and each
   entry of a row in page order, under its row key followed by the row's zero-based position in
   brackets, as `unit_id[0]`.
2. Leave out every figure of a section listed under "Report sections outside the digest", and
   every figure whose section and key, with any bracketed position removed, are listed under
   "Report figures outside the digest".
3. Make each remaining figure a list of three: the section's key, the figure's key as step 1
   gives it, and the figure's `value`, or null where it has none.
4. On a page whose `price_table_rule` is `replayed-and-digested`, append one more list:
   `"envelope"`, `"price_table"` and the page's `price_table` object.
5. Write the list of lists as JSON with no whitespace between tokens, object keys in page order
   rather than sorted, each number as the page writes it, and each character outside ASCII as
   itself. A string escapes only the quotation mark, the backslash and control characters, a
   control character as `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\b` or `\f` where it has that form and otherwise as
   `\u` and four lowercase hex digits.
6. Encode that text as UTF-8, take its SHA-256 digest, and keep the first 16 lowercase hex
   digits. They equal the page's `fingerprint` when the page is as it was filed.

The reference implementation below follows those steps and needs only the Python standard
library. Saved as `fingerprint.py`, `python3 fingerprint.py RPTnnnn.json` prints one fingerprint
for each page it is given, in order.

```python
import hashlib
import json
import sys

OUTSIDE_THE_DIGEST = (("goal", "ended_at"), ("goal", "duration_hours"))
SECTIONS_OUTSIDE_THE_DIGEST = ("lessons", "lane_yield")


def figures(page):
    for section in page.get("sections") or []:
        name = section["key"]
        if section.get("not_measured"):
            yield name, "not_measured", section["not_measured"]
        for key, figure in (section.get("figures") or {}).items():
            yield name, key, figure
        for rows in ("rows", "unit_rows"):
            for i, row in enumerate(section.get(rows) or []):
                for key, figure in row.items():
                    yield name, f"{key}[{i}]", figure


def fingerprint(page):
    payload = [[name, key, figure.get("value")] for name, key, figure in figures(page)
               if name not in SECTIONS_OUTSIDE_THE_DIGEST
               and (name, key.split("[", 1)[0]) not in OUTSIDE_THE_DIGEST]
    if page.get("price_table_rule") == "replayed-and-digested":
        payload.append(["envelope", "price_table", page.get("price_table")])
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for path in sys.argv[1:]:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            print(fingerprint(json.load(handle)))
```

#### Report figures outside the digest

The run's own lifecycle, set by closing and sealing rather than derived from the work: in the
digest, sealing the run would move the fingerprint the page had just recorded. A check compares them with the run
record instead.

| Section | Figure | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `goal` | `ended_at` | The run's end, part of the lifecycle the close and the seal set. |
| `goal` | `duration_hours` | The run's length, measured to the same end. |

#### Report sections outside the digest

Whole sections read from stores that move after the run; the page still shows them as the close
left them.

| Section | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `lessons` | It reads the lesson class store, which every later close moves. |
| `lane_yield` | It reads a log held in one clone, whose refusals are classed by commits that land later. |

### Report schema 1

The first report shape. No writer produces it now, so only pages already filed carry it, and
they cannot be re-derived: each stands as filed. Its pages come in two shapes, the later adding
`waivers`, and the earliest lacks `window_end` in the envelope. The tables below are the whole
of schema 1; its figure keys are not catalogued.

#### Report schema 1 sections

| Section | Title | Emitted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `identity` | Identity | always |
| `header` | Filing | always |
| `goal` | Sprint goal | always |
| `guardrail` | Ship guardrail | always |
| `delivered` | Delivered | always |
| `cost` | Cost | always |
| `accuracy` | Estimate accuracy | always |
| `dora` | DORA | always |
| `units` | Evidence by unit | always |
| `not_proven` | Not proven | always |
| `waivers` | Waivers in force | optional |
| `judges` | Who judged this | always |
| `consult` | Stakeholder consult | always |
| `carried` | Carried open | always |
| `signoff` | Sign-off | always |
| `provenance` | Provenance | always |

#### Report schema 1 envelope keys

| Key | Presence |
| --- | --- |
| `schema` | always |
| `report_id` | always |
| `run_id` | always |
| `retro_id` | always |
| `generated_at` | always |
| `window_end` | optional |
| `signature` | always |
| `sections` | always |
| `fingerprint` | always |

## Run record

`sprint close` files the run's record as `sdlc-studio/reports/runs/<run id>.json`, committed
beside the report, and `sprint sign` and `sprint stop` file it again. It is a JSON object: the
run's state as the last of them held it, so any clone can tell a run awaiting its signature from
a signed one without the checkout that closed it. A path under the project root is written
relative to the root; any other absolute path is written as `sha256:` and the first 12 hex
digits of the path's digest.

The record holds many keys from many writers and gains keys between releases. The tables below
contract the keys a consumer reads, and a parser tolerates any key they do not name. Records
filed by an earlier release stay in the tree as filed, so a parser also meets records without a
key added since: `report_window_end`, `verified_sha` and `plan_digest` are the ones an older
record lacks.

### Run record states

| State | Reached by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Awaiting` | `sprint close` | The close filed the record and nobody has signed the run. |
| `Sealed` | `sprint sign` | The run is signed, and the record carries the signature. |
| `Stopped` | `sprint stop`, after the close | The run ended without a signature, so it awaits nothing. |

### Run record keys

Each state's cell names the JSON type the key holds in that state: `string`, `integer`,
`object`, `list` or `null`, or two of them joined by `or`. A dash means the key is not
contracted in that state and may be absent.

| Key | Awaiting | Sealed | Stopped | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | integer | integer | integer | The record's schema, `1`. |
| `run_id` | string | string | string | The run's id, which names the record's file. |
| `outcome` | string | string | string | `running` while the record awaits its signature; once it is sealed or stopped, how the run ended: `goal-reached`, `budget-spent`, `blocked`, `stopped`, `closed-outstanding`, `partial` or `missed`. |
| `started_at` | string | string | string | When the run opened, an ISO 8601 time. |
| `ended_at` | null | string | string | When the run ended, an ISO 8601 time; null until it is signed or stopped. |
| `sprint_goal` | string | string | string | The goal the run was planned to. |
| `sprint_goal_verdict` | object | object | object | The verdict the goal was judged, with its note. |
| `batch` | list | list | list | The ids of the run's units. |
| `report` | string | string | string | The id of the report the close filed for the run. |
| `report_fingerprint` | string | string | string | That report's fingerprint, which a signature is over. |
| `report_window_end` | string | string | string | The end of the window that report measured to. |
| `close_tree` | string | string | string | The digest of the tree the close ran against; `sprint sign` refuses a tree changed since. |
| `verified_sha` | string | string | string | The commit the close's gate ran against. |
| `plan_digest` | string | string | string | `sha256:` and the 64 hex digits of the sprint plan the run was opened from, which matches a copy of that plan wherever it turns up. |
| `plan` | null | null | null | Null wherever `plan_digest` is written. An older record holds `sha256:` and 12 hex digits, a digest of the plan's path, or the path `sdlc-studio/.local/sprint-plan.json`; neither identifies the plan's content. |
| `plan_snapshot` | object | object | object | The units, points and forecast rates as planned, which the report's estimates read. |
| `reopened` | list | list | list | One entry for each `sprint reopen` of the run; empty when it was never reopened. |
| `signature` | - | object | - | The signature, with the fields below. |
| `stop` | - | - | object | How the run was stopped and why. |

### Run record signature fields

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `principal` | string | Who signed. |
| `signed_at` | string | When, an ISO 8601 time. |
| `report` | string | The report signed. |
| `fingerprint` | string | The fingerprint signed, which matches the report's. |

### Run record awaiting rule

A record awaits its signature when every row below holds; it keeps awaiting until `sprint sign`
seals it. Since D0503 (US1290), `sprint plan --write` no longer refuses on this rule: it opens the
next run over a closed run that awaits. Carrying no signature is not enough: a run the close filed
and `sprint stop` then ended carries none, and awaits nothing.

| Key | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `outcome` | `running` |
| `report` | any non-empty value |

The rule reads the committed record alone, so it has one gap: between a `sprint reopen` and the
next close the record still reads as it was last filed, sealed or stopped.

## Lesson class store

`sdlc-studio/lessons.jsonl` holds one JSON object per line, one line per failure class.
`retro.py extract` writes a new line for a retro's Try item tagged `[new: <class>]`, and adds a
hit to the class's line for one tagged with the class's id. A store that does not exist yet
starts from the classes the skill ships. A field marked **Required** is on every line the writer
produces; the others appear when they apply. A parser tolerates a field neither table names.

### Lesson class row fields

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | yes | The class's id: `LC-` and three or more digits. |
| `class` | yes | The class's name. |
| `rule` | yes | The rule the class states. |
| `behaviour` | yes | What to do differently. |
| `inject` | yes | The phases whose output carries the class: some of `plan`, `build` and `review`. |
| `hits` | yes | The class's repeats, each an object with the fields below; empty until one is recorded. |
| `state` | yes | `active`, `graduating`, `graduated` or `retired`. |
| `recorded_run` | yes | The run the class was recorded in. |
| `recorded_source` | yes | The item that recorded it, so reading that item again is not counted as a repeat. |
| `cr` | no | The change request the class graduated to, once it is graduating. |
| `retired_run` | no | The run the class was retired in. |

### Lesson hit fields

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | yes | The run the repeat is counted against. |
| `unit` | yes | The unit it was found on; empty when none was named. |
| `source` | yes | Where it was read from, such as `retro:` and the retro's id. |
| `finding` | no | The review finding that named the class, when a review recorded the repeat. |

## Evidence logs

The run evidence is committed as JSON lines under `sdlc-studio/retros/evidence/`, one file per
shard: `actuals-<date>.jsonl`, `forecasts-<date>.jsonl` and `audit-cost-<date>.jsonl`, each
dated by the UTC day it was written. The actuals and forecast shard named `0000-migrated` holds
lines moved in from an older release's logs. A parser reads every shard of a log. A field marked **Required** is on
every line the writer produces now; an optional field is omitted when it was not supplied, and a
parser tolerates a field the tables do not name.

### Actuals line fields

`telemetry.py record` appends one line per call, for one unit.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | no | The unit the line measures. |
| `type` | no | The unit's type, such as `story` or `bug`. |
| `iterations` | no | Its build iterations. |
| `wall_time_s` | no | Its wall time in seconds. |
| `stages` | no | The stages it passed through, as recorded. |
| `critic_verdict` | no | The reviewer's verdict on it. |
| `complexity` | no | Its complexity score. |
| `churn` | no | Its churn, as recorded. |
| `reopened` | no | Whether it was reopened, as recorded. |
| `tokens` | no | The tokens it cost. |
| `tier_recommended` | no | The model tier the routing recommended for it. |
| `tier_delivered` | no | The model tier that delivered it. |
| `model` | no | The model that delivered it. |
| `escalated` | no | Whether it escalated to another tier, as recorded. |
| `attempts` | no | One object for each model invocation on the unit, in order, with its `model` and `tokens`; a line without it reads as a single attempt. |
| `project` | yes | The project the line was written in, stamped at write time; `unknown` where it could not be resolved. |

### Forecast line fields

`sprint plan` writes one line for each unit it forecasts, and `telemetry.py forecast` writes one
by hand. A forecast with the same tokens and constants as one already held for the unit is not
written again.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | yes | The unit forecast. |
| `tokens` | yes | The tokens forecast for it. |
| `points` | no | The size the plan recorded. |
| `seed` | no | The seed the estimate started from. |
| `seed_source` | no | Where that seed came from. |
| `complexity` | no | The unit's complexity score at plan time. |
| `estimator` | no | Who made the size call. |
| `size_gate` | no | `compulsory` or `voluntary`: the size gate the plan applied. |
| `constants` | yes | The estimator's constants, by name, as integers. |
| `planned_at` | yes | When the forecast was made, an ISO 8601 time. |
| `project` | yes | The project the line was written in, stamped at write time. |
| `effort` | no | The size on a line written when sizes were Efforts; no writer produces it now. |
| `effort_gate` | no | The earlier name of `size_gate`; no writer produces it now. |

### Audit cost line fields

`audit_cost.py record` writes one line for each finished audit run. Every field it captures is
written on every line, as null where nothing was supplied.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | yes | The day the run was recorded. |
| `run_id` | yes | The audit run's id, or null. |
| `provenance` | yes | `recorded` for a run measured when it finished, or `backfilled` for one asserted from earlier prose. |
| `lenses` | yes | The lenses the run covered. |
| `rounds` | yes | The round cap it used. |
| `votes` | yes | The refute-panel votes for each candidate. |
| `estimated_agents` | yes | The agents the estimate predicted. |
| `estimated_tokens` | yes | The tokens the estimate predicted. |
| `actual_agents` | yes | The agents the run used. |
| `actual_tokens` | yes | The tokens the run cost. |
| `actual_minutes` | yes | The wall minutes it took, or null. |
| `notes` | yes | A note, or null. |
| `project` | no | The project, on a line stamped after it was written. |

## Ledgers

Four ledgers are Markdown tables a writer appends to, or rewrites, under a fixed header row. The
tables below give each header's columns in order; a parser locates the header by its first
column's name.

### Critic ledger columns

`critic.py record` appends one row per review verdict to `sdlc-studio/reviews/critic-verdicts.md`,
and the latest row for a unit is the one in force.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Unit` | The unit reviewed. |
| `Verdict` | `APPROVE`, or `REJECT` for a unit to repair before it is Done. |
| `Reviewer` | Who reviewed it; a row whose reviewer is the unit's author never clears the Done gate. |
| `Author` | Who wrote it. |
| `Date` | When the verdict was recorded. |
| `Brief` | The brief the reviewer was given; a hand-written prompt records none. |
| `Tier` | The review depth, `full` or `light`, then a space and `(explicit)` when the operator chose it with `--tier-explicit`; `-` when the verdict recorded none. |
| `Source` | `sha256:`, 16 hex digits and the file name of the brief the review read, then any later tokens; `-` when the verdict was transcribed. |
| `Issues` | The issues the reviewer raised. |

Rows written before a column existed are kept as written, never padded or rewritten, so a parser
meets narrower rows too, read by their cell count:

| Cells | Columns |
| --- | --- |
| 8 | `Unit`, `Verdict`, `Reviewer`, `Author`, `Date`, `Brief`, `Tier`, `Issues` |
| 7 | `Unit`, `Verdict`, `Reviewer`, `Author`, `Date`, `Brief`, `Issues` |
| 6 | `Unit`, `Verdict`, `Reviewer`, `Author`, `Date`, `Issues` |
| 5 | `Unit`, `Verdict`, `Reviewer`, `Date`, `Issues` |

### Velocity history columns

`retro.py accuracy --write` keeps `sdlc-studio/retros/VELOCITY.md`, one row per retro, and
rewrites the whole table when it records a row. An absent figure reads `-`. The reader indexes
the columns by their names in the header row, so read them by name.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Retro` | The retro the row records. |
| `Date` | The retro's date. |
| `Units` | The units in the sprint's batch. |
| `Measured` | The units with a measured cost. |
| `Forecast` | The units the plan forecast. |
| `Points` | The points delivered: the velocity. |
| `Written` | The points the sprint produced, adding units whose code shipped and was reviewed but not accepted. |
| `Estimate (tokens, plan-time)` | The forecast as recorded when the sprint was planned. |
| `Actual (tokens)` | What the sprint cost; empty when it was not measured, with the reason in `Note`. |
| `Ratio (est/actual)` | The estimate over the actual; `-` where none was formed, as for a sprint that mixed models. |
| `Tokens/pt` | The actual over the points, where both cover the same units. |
| `Priced/pt` | The priced cost per point, in input-equivalent tokens. |
| `Oversized` | The units delivered above the split threshold. |
| `Wall (s)` | The wall time in seconds. |
| `Overhead` | Overhead time against delivery time. |
| `Overhead bound` | `exact` when every component of the overhead was measured, `lower` when the ratio is a floor. |
| `Constants` | The estimator that made the forecast. |
| `Sample` | Whether the constants were fitted to this sprint, in sample, or not, out of sample. |
| `Model` | The model that delivered the sprint, or `mixed`. |
| `Note` | Why a figure is absent or qualified. |
| `Source` | Where `Actual (tokens)` was read from, such as `per-unit`, `harness` or `supplied`. |

### Decisions ledger columns

`decisions.py add` keeps `sdlc-studio/decisions.md`, creating it from the shipped template when
it is absent.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ID` | The decision's id. |
| `Decision` | What was decided. |
| `Rationale` | Why, with the markers below on a waiver. |
| `Status` | `accepted`, `superseded` or `revisited`. |
| `Supersedes` | The decision it replaces, or empty. |
| `Date` | When it was recorded. |

A waiver's `Rationale` cell may carry two markers: `[kind: deliberate]` or `[kind: expired]`,
then `[authorised by: <who>]`, which is always last in the cell. Any other bracketed text in the
cell is not contracted.

### Deploy log columns

`deploy.py record` appends one row per deploy outcome to `sdlc-studio/deploy-log.md`, creating
it when it is absent.

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `When` | When the outcome was recorded, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` in local time. |
| `Status` | `rolled-out`, `verified`, `rolled-back` or `failed`. |
| `Detail` | What happened. |
